questions.question: Which of the following features enables simple squamous epithelium to efficiently carry out diffusion?

options.text: Flat, thin, and closely packed cells
Presence of multiple layers of cells

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flat, thin, and closely packed cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Simple squamous epithelium** is a single layer of **flat, thin, and closely packed cells** that resemble floor tiles when viewed from above. Their extremely thin profile creates a minimal barrier, which is essential for the rapid **diffusion** of gases and **filtration** of liquids across the membrane. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Cells with **thick cytoplasm and large nuclei** (Statement 1) are typically characteristic of **cuboidal** or **columnar epithelium**. These cells are more involved in metabolic activities, **secretion**, and **absorption** rather than passive diffusion, as the increased thickness would slow down the movement of molecules. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The presence of **cilia** (Statement 2) is a specialized feature of **ciliated epithelium**. These hair-like structures are used to move **mucus** or particles across the surface of the tissue, such as in the **respiratory tract** or **fallopian tubes**, and do not directly assist in the process of diffusion. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **presence of multiple layers** of cells (Statement 4) describes **stratified epithelium**. This structure is designed for **protection** against mechanical or chemical stress (like in the **skin**) and is too thick to allow for efficient diffusion. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Because the cells are **closely packed** with very little **intercellular matrix**, they form a continuous surface that acts as a selective **permeable membrane**, allowing specific small molecules like **oxygen** and **carbon dioxide** to pass through easily.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Locations of Simple Squamous Epithelium:**
 
 
• **Alveoli of the Lungs:** Where **gas exchange** occurs between the air and the blood.
 
• **Endothelium:** The lining of **blood vessels** and **lymphatic vessels**, facilitating the exchange of nutrients and waste.
 
• **Mesothelium:** The epithelial component of **serous membranes** lining the body cavities (pleura, pericardium, and peritoneum).
 
• **Bowman's Capsule:** Found in the **kidneys**, where it aids in the **filtration** of blood to form urine.
 
 
 
• **Primary Functions:**
 
 
• **Diffusion:** Allows for the movement of molecules from an area of **high concentration** to **low concentration**.
 
• **Osmosis:** The movement of water through the thin membrane.
 
• **Filtration:** Passing fluids through a biological "sieve" to remove larger particles or cells.
 
 
 
• **Structural Characteristics:**
 
 
• The cells are often described as **pavement epithelium** due to their appearance.
 
• Each cell has a **centrally located**, oval or flattened **nucleus** that bulges slightly.
 
• The tissue is **avascular**, meaning it does not contain its own blood vessels and relies on **diffusion** from underlying **connective tissue** for nutrients.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Epithelial Tissue Classification:** Tissues are classified based on the **number of layers** (Simple vs. Stratified) and the **shape of the cells** (Squamous, Cuboidal, or Columnar).
 
• **Simple Epithelium:** Consists of a **single layer** of cells and is found where absorption, secretion, and filtration occur.
 
• **Stratified Epithelium:** Consists of **two or more layers** and is primarily found in areas subject to **wear and tear**, providing high-level **protection**.
 
• **Basement Membrane:** All epithelial tissues rest on a non-cellular **basement membrane**, which provides structural support and attaches the epithelium to the underlying tissue.
</ul

questions.question: What was the primary goal of the Chipko Movement of the Garhwal region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protection of the forest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chipko Movement** was a non-violent, social, and ecological movement by rural villagers, particularly women, in **India** during the **1970s**.
 
• The primary objective of the movement was the **protection of the forest** from **commercial logging** and **deforestation** authorized by the government. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• It originated in the **Garhwal Himalayas** of **Uttarakhand** (then part of Uttar Pradesh) in **1973** and quickly spread throughout the Himalayan region.
 
• The name of the movement comes from the word **'chipko'**, which means **'to hug'** or **'to stick'** in Hindi, reflecting the protesters' method of **hugging trees** to prevent them from being cut down.
 
• The movement was a landmark in **environmentalism** as it highlighted that the livelihood of local communities depends on the health of the **natural ecosystem**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Figures:** 
 
 
• **Sunderlal Bahuguna**: An environmentalist who gave the movement a proper direction and appealed to the **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi**, which resulted in a **15-year ban** on cutting green trees in the Himalayan forests in **1980**.
 
• **Chandi Prasad Bhatt**: One of the pioneers who organized the local cooperative organization **Dasholi Gram Swarajya Sangh** (DGSS) to help locals utilize forest resources sustainably.
 
• **Gaura Devi**: A prominent woman leader who organized the women of **Reni village** to stop the felling of trees when the men were away.
 
 
 
• **Inspiration:** The movement was inspired by the **Bishnoi community** of **Rajasthan**. In the **1730s**, **Amrita Devi** and 363 others sacrificed their lives to protect **Khejri trees** from being cut down by the orders of the Maharaja of Jodhpur.
 
• **Global Impact:** The Chipko Movement is often regarded as one of the first **eco-feminist** movements in the world because of the massive participation of women. It won the **Right Livelihood Award** in **1987** for its dedication to the conservation and restoration of India's natural resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ecological Slogan:** Sunderlal Bahuguna coined the famous slogan: **"Ecology is permanent economy"**, emphasizing that long-term economic stability relies on environmental health.
 
• **Outcome:** Apart from the 15-year ban on commercial felling in the **Himalayas**, the movement led to the creation of the **Forest Conservation Act of 1980** in India and a significant shift in India’s **forest policy** from revenue generation to **conservation**.
 
• **Geographic Reach:** While it started in the **Chamoli district**, its success inspired similar movements across the country, such as the **Appiko Movement** in **Karnataka** in **1983**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about Ohm’s law?

options.text: Current is inversely proportional to voltage at constant temperature.
Resistance remains constant only for non-ohmic conductors.
Ohm’s law is applicable to all materials at all temperatures.
Current is directly proportional to voltage at constant temperature.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Current is directly proportional to voltage at constant temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ohm’s Law** states that the **electric current** (I) flowing through a conductor is **directly proportional** to the **potential difference** (V) across its ends, provided physical conditions like **temperature** remain constant.
 
• The mathematical expression for this relationship is **V = IR**, where **R** is the **Resistance** of the conductor.
 
• **Statement 1**: It claims current is inversely proportional to voltage. According to the formula **I = V/R**, current increases as voltage increases. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2**: It suggests resistance remains constant only for non-ohmic conductors. In reality, resistance is constant for **Ohmic conductors**, while for **non-ohmic** conductors (like semiconductors), resistance varies with voltage or current. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 3**: It says the law is applicable to all materials at all temperatures. However, **Ohm’s law** is not universal; it does not apply to **insulators**, **semiconductors**, or **vacuum tubes**, and it fails if the **temperature** changes significantly. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4**: It correctly identifies the core principle that **Current (I)** is **directly proportional** to **Voltage (V)** at a **constant temperature**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Current is directly proportional to voltage at constant temperature.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context**: The law was named after the **German physicist Georg Simon Ohm**, who published his findings in **1827** in his book "The Galvanic Circuit Investigated Mathematically."
 
• **Units of Measurement**: 
 
 
• **Voltage (V)** is measured in **Volts**.
 
• **Current (I)** is measured in **Amperes (A)**.
 
• **Resistance (R)** is measured in **Ohms (Ω)**.
 
 
 
• **Ohmic vs. Non-Ohmic Conductors**:
 
 
• **Ohmic Conductors**: These materials follow Ohm’s Law strictly. Examples include **copper**, **silver**, and **aluminum** under normal operating conditions. The **V-I graph** for these materials is a **straight line** passing through the origin.
 
• **Non-Ohmic Conductors**: These materials do not show a linear relationship between V and I. Examples include **diodes**, **transistors**, **LEDs**, and **electrolytes**. Their resistance changes as the applied voltage changes.
 
 
 
• **Resistance Factors**: The resistance of a conductor depends on its **length**, **area of cross-section**, **nature of the material**, and **temperature**. Generally, the resistance of metals **increases** with an **increase** in **temperature**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Experimental Verification**: When a graph is plotted between **Potential Difference (V)** on the y-axis and **Current (I)** on the x-axis, the slope of the **straight line** represents the **Resistance (R)** of the conductor.
 
• **Limitations of Ohm’s Law**:
 
 
• It is not applicable to **unilateral networks** (circuits where current flows in only one direction, like those with diodes).
 
• It is not applicable to **non-linear elements** where the current does not change linearly with voltage (like **thyristors**).
 
• The law only holds true if **physical parameters** such as **temperature**, **strain**, and **pressure** are kept **constant**.
 
 
 
• **Applications**: Ohm’s law is fundamental for determining the **voltage**, **current**, or **resistance** in a linear electric circuit. It is used extensively in **electrical engineering**, designing **domestic appliances**, and calculating the **power consumption** of electrical devices.

questions.question: In wastewater treatment plant, the biogas is obtained from which of the following substance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sludge**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP)**, **Sludge** is the organic solid material that settles at the bottom of **Sedimentation Tanks** during the treatment process.
 
• This **Sludge** is transferred to a separate tank where it is decomposed by **Anaerobic Bacteria**. This process is known as **Anaerobic Digestion**.
 
• The byproduct of this biological decomposition is **Biogas**, which is a mixture of gases produced by the breakdown of organic matter in the absence of **Oxygen**.
 
• **Biogas** primarily consists of **Methane (CH4)**, which typically ranges from **50% to 75%**, and **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**, ranging from **25% to 50%**, along with small amounts of **Hydrogen Sulfide** and **Moisture**.
 
• The **Biogas** generated from **Sludge** can be utilized as a **Fuel** for heating or to produce **Electricity** to power the treatment plant itself, making the facility more energy-efficient.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary and Secondary Sludge**: 
 
 
• **Primary Sludge** is obtained during the **Physical Treatment** (primary sedimentation) where heavy solids settle down.
 
• **Secondary Sludge** (also called **Activated Sludge**) is obtained after **Biological Treatment**, where microorganisms consume organic pollutants in **Aeration Tanks**.
 
 
 
• **Wastewater Treatment Process**:
 
 
• The process involves **Screening** (removal of large objects), **Grit Removal** (settling of sand and pebbles), **Primary Clarification** (settling of organic solids), and **Secondary Treatment** (aeration and biological breakdown).
 
• After the **Sludge** is digested and **Biogas** is extracted, the remaining solid matter is dried and used as **Manure** or **Fertilizer** because it is rich in organic matter and nutrients like **Nitrogen** and **Phosphorus**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Analysis**:
 
 
• **Coconut Husk**, **Dried Leaves**, and **Banana Peels** are forms of **Biomass** or **Municipal Solid Waste**. While they can be used in specialized **Biogas Plants** (like **Gobar Gas** plants) through composting or digestion, they are not the specific substances from which biogas is extracted within a standard **Wastewater Treatment Plant**.
 
• **Sludge** is specifically the byproduct of **Sewage** and **Industrial Wastewater** processing.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**:
 
 
• Capturing **Biogas** from **Sludge** prevents the release of **Methane**, a potent **Greenhouse Gas**, into the atmosphere, thereby helping in the mitigation of **Climate Change**.
 
• The **Clean Water Act** and various environmental guidelines in **India**, managed by the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**, mandate the proper treatment of sewage to protect water bodies from **Eutrophication**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The Tyndall effect is observed when:

options.text: light is absorbed by particles in a solution
light reflects from a mirror surface
light is scattered by very fine particles suspended in a medium

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**light is scattered by very fine particles suspended in a medium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Tyndall effect** is a physical phenomenon where **light beams** are scattered by particles in a **colloid** or a very fine **suspension**.
 
• It is observed when the size of the individual particles is comparable to the **wavelength** of the light, typically ranging between **1 nanometer** and **1000 nanometers**.
 
• The effect was first described in detail by the **Irish physicist John Tyndall** in the **year 1869**. It helps in distinguishing between a **true solution** and a **colloidal solution**.
 
• When a beam of light passes through a **colloid**, the suspended particles scatter the light, making the **path of the beam** visible to the observer. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 3.***

questions.question: A mixture differs from a compound in that:

options.text: it has fixed proportions of elements

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**its components retain their properties**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **mixture** is a substance made by combining two or more different materials in such a way that no **chemical reaction** occurs. In a mixture, each constituent substance **retains its own chemical identity** and properties. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Unlike a **compound**, which has a **fixed ratio** of atoms, the components of a mixture can be present in **variable proportions**. For example, a sugar solution can be dilute or concentrated depending on the amount of sugar added. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• A mixture does not show "combined" or entirely new properties; rather, it exhibits the **individual properties** of its parts. If you mix **iron filings** and **sulfur powder**, the iron still remains magnetic and can be pulled away with a magnet. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The components of a mixture can be separated by **physical methods** such as **filtration**, **distillation**, **crystallization**, or **magnetism** because they are not chemically bonded. In contrast, compounds can only be separated into elements through **chemical reactions**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The formation of a mixture is a **physical change** and usually involves **no energy change** (absorption or evolution of heat/light) during the mixing process, whereas compound formation is a **chemical change** often accompanied by energy transfer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Mixtures:**
 
 
• **Homogeneous Mixtures:** These have a **uniform composition** throughout. Examples include **air** (a mixture of gases like **nitrogen**, **oxygen**, and **carbon dioxide**) and **alloys** like **brass** (copper and zinc).
 
• **Heterogeneous Mixtures:** These have **non-uniform compositions** where the different components can often be seen with the naked eye or a microscope. Examples include **oil and water**, **sand and salt**, or **blood**.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Compounds:**
 
 
• A **compound** is a substance formed when two or more elements are **chemically bonded** together.
 
• The **properties** of a compound are **entirely different** from its constituent elements. For instance, **water (H2O)** is a liquid used to extinguish fires, but it is made of **hydrogen** (highly flammable gas) and **oxygen** (supporter of combustion).
 
• Compounds follow the **Law of Definite Proportions**, meaning they always contain the same elements in the **same mass ratio**.
 
 
 
• **Separation Techniques:**
 
 
• **Centrifugation:** Used for separating denser particles from lighter particles in a liquid (e.g., separating **cream from milk**).

• **Fractional Distillation:** Used to separate miscible liquids with **boiling point differences** of less than **25 K**, such as components of **petroleum** or **liquid air**.
 
 
 
• **Key Examples:**
 
 
• **Gunpowder:** A mixture of **potassium nitrate (75%)**, **charcoal (15%)**, and **sulfur (10%)**.

• **Chemical vs Physical Identity:** The most fundamental difference lies in the **identity** of the atoms. In a **mixture**, atoms exist side-by-side. In a **compound**, atoms are rearranged into **molecules** or **ionic lattices** with new **chemical bonds**.
 
• **Melting and Boiling Points:** **Pure compounds** have **sharp and fixed** melting and boiling points, whereas **mixtures** often melt or boil over a **range of temperatures** depending on their composition.
 
• **Energy:** Formation of a mixture is **not accompanied** by a net chemical energy change, whereas the formation of a compound involves **breaking old bonds and forming new ones**, releasing or absorbing **enthalpy**.

questions.question: Why is graphite a good conductor of electricity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It has free-moving electrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Graphite** is a naturally occurring **allotrope** of **carbon** that exhibits unique physical and chemical properties due to its internal structure.
 
• In the **atomic structure** of graphite, each **carbon atom** is covalently bonded to only **three** other carbon atoms in a **hexagonal planar** arrangement.
 
• Carbon has **four valence electrons**. Since only **three** are used for bonding in graphite, the **fourth electron** remains **unbonded** and is **delocalized**.
 
• These **delocalized electrons** are **free to move** throughout the **hexagonal layers** of the crystal lattice. ***Hence, the statement that it has free-moving electrons is correct.***
 
• The presence of these **mobile electrons** allows graphite to conduct **electricity** efficiently, making it an exception among non-metals, which are generally poor conductors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hybridization and Bonding**: 
 
 
• In graphite, the **carbon atoms** undergo **sp2 hybridization**. 
 
• The **covalent bonds** within the **hexagonal rings** are extremely strong, contributing to graphite's high **stability** and a **melting point** of approximately **3600°C to 3900°C**.
 
 
 
• **Physical State and Lubrication**: 
 
 
• Graphite consists of multiple **layers** or **sheets**. These layers are held together by weak **Van der Waals forces**.
 
• Because these forces are weak, the layers can **slide** over one another, giving graphite its **soft**, **slippery**, and **greasy** feel. 
 
• This property makes it an excellent **dry lubricant** for machines operating at high **temperatures**.
 
 
 
• **Applications**: 
 
 
• **Electrodes**: Due to its high **electrical conductivity** and **heat resistance**, it is used to make **electrodes** for **electric arc furnaces** and **batteries**.
 
• **Pencils**: It is mixed with **clay** to create the "lead" in **pencils**.
 
• **Nuclear Reactors**: High-purity graphite is used as a **neutron moderator** to slow down fast-moving neutrons in **nuclear power plants**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Diamond**: 
 
 
• Unlike graphite, **Diamond** involves **sp3 hybridization** where all **four valence electrons** are used to form **strong covalent bonds** in a **tetrahedral** structure. 
 
• Because there are no **free electrons** in its structure, diamond is an **insulator** (a very poor conductor of electricity).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Anisotropy**: The **conductivity** of graphite is **anisotropic**, meaning it conducts **electricity** much better **parallel** to its layers than **perpendicular** to them.
 
• **Chemical Inertness**: Graphite is chemically **inert** to most **acids** and **alkalis** under normal conditions, which increases its utility in **industrial applications** involving **corrosive** environments.
 
• **Color and Lustre**: It is a **greyish-black**, **opaque** substance with a **metallic lustre**.
 
• **Density**: The **density** of graphite is approximately **2.26 g/cm³**, which is lower than that of diamond (**3.51 g/cm³**) because of the **large spacing** between its layers.

questions.question: An electric geyser has a power of 2200 { W} when it is operated at 220 { V} . How much will be the current flowing through the heater?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **electric power (P)** of an appliance is defined as the rate at which electrical energy is consumed or converted into other forms of energy (such as heat or light). It is measured in the **SI unit** of **Watt (W)**.
 
• The mathematical relationship between **power (P)**, **voltage (V)**, and **electric current (I)** is expressed by the formula **P = V × I**.
 
• In the given problem, the **power** of the electric geyser is **2200 W** and the **potential difference (voltage)** at which it operates is **220 V**.
 
• To find the **current (I)** flowing through the heating element, we rearrange the formula to **I = P / V**.
 
• Substituting the given numerical values: **I = 2200 / 220**. By performing the division, we get **I = 10 A**. This signifies that a current of **10 Amperes** flows through the geyser when it is operational.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 10 A.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Current (I):**
 
 
• It is the rate of flow of **electric charge** through a cross-section of a conductor. The **SI unit** is the **Ampere (A)**, which is equivalent to **one Coulomb per second (1 C/s)**.
 
• The instrument used to measure the magnitude of current in a circuit is called an **Ammeter**, which is always connected in **series**.
 
 
 
• **Voltage (V):**
 
 
• Also known as **electric potential difference**, it is the work done in moving a unit positive charge from one point to another. Its **SI unit** is the **Volt (V)**.
 
• A **Voltmeter** is used to measure the potential difference and is always connected in **parallel** across the points where the voltage is to be measured.
 
 
 
• **Resistance (R) and Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• **Resistance** is the property of a conductor to resist the flow of charges through it. Its **SI unit** is the **Ohm (Ω)**.
 
• According to **Ohm's Law**, the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage across it (**V = I × R**), provided physical conditions like **temperature** remain constant.
 
• For the geyser in the question, the **resistance** of the coil can be calculated as **R = V / I = 220 / 10 = 22 Ω**.
 
 
 
• **Joule's Law of Heating:**
 
 
• Electric geysers work on the principle of the **heating effect of electric current**. When current passes through a high-resistance wire, electrical energy is converted into **heat energy**.
 
• The heat produced **(H)** is given by **H = I²Rt**, where **I** is current, **R** is resistance, and **t** is the time for which the current flows.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Power Variations:** Power can also be calculated using the formulas **P = I²R** or **P = V² / R** depending on the known variables in a circuit.
 
• **Commercial Unit of Energy:** While the **Watt** is the unit of power, the commercial unit of electrical energy is the **kilowatt-hour (kWh)**, often referred to as a "unit." **1 kWh** is equal to **3.6 × 10⁶ Joules**.
 
• **Safety Devices:** For high-power appliances like a **2200 W** geyser, using a **fuse** or a **Miniature Circuit Breaker (MCB)** with an appropriate rating (e.g., **15 A** or **16 A**) is essential to prevent electrical fires due to **overloading**.

questions.question: Starting from rest, a car attains a velocity of 10 m/s in 20 s. Braking reduces the velocity to 5 m/s in the next 5 s. What is the respective acceleration in the two scenarios?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.5 m/s² ; -1 m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **first scenario**, the car starts from **rest**, which means its **initial velocity (u)** is **0 m/s**. It reaches a **final velocity (v)** of **10 m/s** within a **time (t)** of **20 seconds**.
 
• The formula for **acceleration (a)** is derived from the first equation of motion: **a = (v - u) / t**. By substituting the values, we get **a = (10 - 0) / 20**, which equals **0.5 m/s²**.
 
• In the **second scenario**, the car is already moving at **10 m/s**, making this the new **initial velocity (u)**. Braking reduces its **final velocity (v)** to **5 m/s** over a period of **5 seconds**.
 
• Applying the same formula for the second scenario, **a = (5 - 10) / 5**, which results in **-5 / 5 = -1 m/s²**. This negative value indicates **retardation**.
 
• The respective accelerations for the two scenarios are **0.5 m/s²** and **-1 m/s²**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Acceleration**: It is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** with respect to **time**. Because it has both magnitude and direction, it is classified as a **vector quantity**.
 
• **SI Unit**: The standard unit for measuring acceleration in the **International System of Units (SI)** is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
• **Retardation or Deceleration**: When the **acceleration** of an object is in the opposite direction of its **velocity**, it is called **negative acceleration** or **retardation**. This occurs when an object slows down, such as when **brakes** are applied to a **vehicle**.
 
• **Uniform vs. Non-Uniform Acceleration**: If the **velocity** changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of **time**, the object is said to have **uniform acceleration**. If the change in velocity is not constant over time, it is **non-uniform**.
 
• **Equations of Motion**: These are mathematical formulas that describe the behavior of a physical system in terms of its motion. The primary equations include **v = u + at**, **s = ut + ½at²**, and **v² = u² + 2as**, where **s** represents **displacement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Initial Velocity (u)**: When a body starts from **rest**, its **u** is always taken as **0**. Conversely, if a body comes to a **stop**, its **final velocity (v)** is **0**.
 
• **Direction of Acceleration**: If the **velocity** and **acceleration** are in the same direction, the speed of the object increases. If they are in opposite directions, the speed decreases.
 
• **Graphic Representation**: On a **Velocity-Time graph**, the **slope** of the line represents the **acceleration** of the object. A positive slope indicates **acceleration**, while a negative slope indicates **deceleration**.
 
• **Numerical Values**: In the given problem, the calculation shows a clear transition from a **positive acceleration** of **0.5 m/s²** during the speeding-up phase to a **negative acceleration** of **-1 m/s²** during the braking phase.

questions.question: If the value of the Universal Gravitational Constant (G), the mass of the Earth (M), and the radius of the Earth (R) are known, which equation is used to calculate the acceleration due to gravity (g) near the Earth's surface?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**g = GM/R²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between **acceleration due to gravity (g)** and the **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)** is derived from **Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation** and **Newton’s Second Law of Motion**.
 
• According to the Law of Universal Gravitation, the force of attraction **(F)** between the Earth (mass **M**) and an object (mass **m**) on its surface is given by **F = G(Mm/R²)**, where **R** is the **radius of the Earth**.
 
• According to Newton’s Second Law, the force acting on the object is also its weight, expressed as **F = mg**, where **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity**.
 
• By equating the two formulas for force (**mg = GMm/R²**), the mass of the object (**m**) cancels out from both sides, leaving the equation **g = GM/R²**. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• This formula shows that the value of **g** depends only on the **mass of the Earth (M)** and the **radius of the Earth (R)**, and is independent of the mass of the falling object.
 
• The options **g = GR/M²**, **R²/(GM)**, and **g = GM/R** are mathematically and dimensionally inconsistent with the physical laws of gravitation. ***Hence, options 1, 2, and 3 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G):** It is a scalar quantity with a constant value of approximately **6.674 x 10^-11 N m²/kg²**. It was first experimentally determined by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798**.
 
• **Mass of the Earth (M):** The Earth's mass is approximately **5.972 x 10^24 kg**. This value, combined with **G** and **R**, results in the standard gravity we experience.
 
• **Radius of the Earth (R):** The mean radius of the Earth is about **6,371 kilometers** (or **6.4 x 10⁶ meters**). Because the Earth is an **oblate spheroid**, the radius is larger at the **Equator** and smaller at the **Poles**.
 
• **Value of g:** On the surface of the Earth, the standard value of **g** is taken as **9.8 m/s²**. However, since **g** is inversely proportional to **R²**, the value of **g** is **maximum at the Poles** (smallest radius) and **minimum at the Equator** (largest radius).
 
• **Variation with Altitude and Depth:** The value of **g** decreases as we go **higher above the Earth's surface** (altitude increases **R**) and also decreases as we go **down into the Earth** (towards the center), becoming **zero at the center of the Earth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between G and g:** **G** is a **universal constant** that remains the same everywhere in the universe, while **g** is a **vector quantity** that changes depending on the **location** (planet, altitude, or latitude).
 
• **Units and Dimensions:** The **SI unit** of **g** is **m/s²** (same as acceleration), and its dimensional formula is **[M⁰ L¹ T^-2]**.
 
• **Weight vs. Mass:** While **mass** is the amount of matter in an object and remains constant, **weight (W = mg)** is a force that changes if the value of **g** changes (e.g., you would weigh less on the **Moon** where **g** is about **1.62 m/s²**).
 
• **Applications:** This equation is fundamental in **astrophysics** and **space science** to calculate the **escape velocity** of a planet and to determine the **orbital velocity** of satellites.

questions.question: The process of transfer of pollen grains from one flower to the stigma of another flower is called ______.
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**pollination**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pollination** is the biological process of transferring **pollen grains** from the male **anther** of a flower to the female **stigma**. This process is essential for the **fertilization** and production of seeds in **angiosperms** (flowering plants). ***Hence, the correct answer is pollination.***
 
• There are two main types of pollination: **Self-pollination**, where pollen is transferred within the same flower or to another flower on the same plant, and **Cross-pollination**, where pollen is transferred to a flower on a different plant of the same species.
 
• The transfer of pollen requires various agents known as **pollinators**. These can be **biotic** (living) such as **bees**, **butterflies**, **birds**, and **bats**, or **abiotic** (non-living) such as **wind** and **water**.
 
• When pollen lands on a compatible stigma, it begins to grow a **pollen tube** down the style to reach the **ovule**, leading to the fusion of male and female gametes.
 
• Plants have evolved specific features to attract pollinators, including **brightly colored petals**, **scent**, and **nectar**, which serve as a food source for insects and animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Germination**:
 
 
• It is the process by which a **seed** develops into a new **plant** or **seedling**.
 
• This process begins when the seed absorbs **water** (imbibition), causing the seed coat to burst and the **embryo** to resume growth.
 
• Factors required for successful germination include **oxygen**, **moisture**, and an optimum **temperature**.
 
 
 
• **Guttation**:
 
 
• It is the loss of **water** in the form of liquid **droplets** from the margins or tips of leaves of some **vascular plants**.
 
• This occurs through specialized pores called **hydathodes**, usually during the **night** or early **morning** when the humidity is high and soil moisture is abundant.
 
• It is driven by **root pressure** rather than **transpiration**.
 
 
 
• **Gestation**:
 
 
• In biology, **gestation** refers to the period of **development** of an **embryo** or **fetus** inside the mother's **uterus** (womb).
 
• This term is specifically used for **viviparous** animals, primarily **mammals**.
 
• The **gestation period** varies by species; for example, it is approximately **280 days** (9 months) in humans and about **600-660 days** in elephants.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pollination Syndromes**: Different plants use different methods to attract pollinators. **Anemophily** refers to wind pollination, while **Entomophily** refers to pollination by **insects**.
 
• **Fertilization**: While pollination is the physical transfer of pollen, **fertilization** is the actual chemical union of the **sperm** (from pollen) and **egg** (inside the ovule).
 
• **Ecological Importance**: Pollination is a vital **ecosystem service**. Over **75%** of the world's food crops depend, at least in part, on **pollination** by animals.
</ul

questions.question: An atom contains 17 electrons and 18 neutrons. Find the number of protons.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**17**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **atom** is fundamentally neutral in its ground state. This means the total **positive charge** provided by the protons must be exactly balanced by the total **negative charge** provided by the electrons.
 
• The number of **protons** in an atom is known as its **Atomic Number** (represented by the symbol **Z**). It defines the identity of the chemical element.
 
• In the given question, the atom contains **17 electrons**. For the atom to remain electrically neutral, the number of **protons** must be equal to the number of electrons. Therefore, the number of protons is **17**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 17.***
 
• The **neutrons** are subatomic particles found in the nucleus that carry **no charge**. While they contribute to the mass of the atom, they do not influence the count of protons required for electrical neutrality.
 
• The element with **Atomic Number 17** is **Chlorine (Cl)**. In this specific case, with **18 neutrons**, the atom refers to the most common isotope of Chlorine, which is **Chlorine-35**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Subatomic Particles:**
 
 
• **Protons**: These were discovered by **Ernest Rutherford** (though often associated with **E. Goldstein**). They have a relative charge of **+1** and a mass of approximately **1.672 x 10^-27 kg**.
 
• **Electrons**: Discovered by **J.J. Thomson** in **1897** through cathode ray experiments. They have a relative charge of **-1** and a negligible mass compared to nucleons.
 
• **Neutrons**: Discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**. They are neutral (zero charge) and have a mass slightly greater than that of a proton.
 
 
 
• **Mass Number (A):**
 
 
• The **Mass Number** is the sum of the total number of **protons** and **neutrons** present in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• For the given atom: **Mass Number (A) = Protons (17) + Neutrons (18) = 35**.
 
• The total number of protons and neutrons are collectively called **nucleons**.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Notation:**
 
 
• Elements are usually represented as **AXZ**, where **X** is the chemical symbol, **A** is the mass number, and **Z** is the atomic number.
 
• The atom in the question would be represented as **³⁵Cl₁₇**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Isotopes**: These are atoms of the same element (same **Atomic Number**) that have different numbers of **neutrons** (different **Mass Numbers**). For example, Chlorine has isotopes like **Chlorine-35** and **Chlorine-37**.
 
• **Ions**: If an atom gains or loses electrons, it becomes an **ion**. In an ion, the number of **protons** and **electrons** are not equal. However, the number of protons (atomic number) **never changes** during a chemical reaction.
 
• **Valency**: Chlorine has **17 electrons**. Its electronic configuration is **2, 8, 7**. Since it requires **1 electron** to complete its octet, its **valency** is **1**.
 
• **Calculations**:
 
 
• Number of Protons = **Atomic Number (Z)**.
 
• Number of Neutrons = **Mass Number (A) - Atomic Number (Z)**.
 
• In a neutral atom: **Protons = Electrons**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In a 250 mL solution, 5 g of solute is dissolved. What is the concentration (mass by volume %) of the solution?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **concentration of a solution** is the amount of solute present in a given quantity of the solution or solvent. It can be expressed in various ways, including **Mass by Volume Percentage**.
 
• **Mass by Volume Percentage (w/v %)** is defined as the mass of the **solute** in **grams** dissolved in **100 mL** of the **solution**.
 
• In this problem, the mass of the **solute** is given as **5 g**.
 
• The total **volume of the solution** is given as **250 mL**.
 
• The mathematical formula to calculate this concentration is: **Concentration = (Mass of Solute / Volume of Solution) x 100**.
 
• Substituting the given values: **(5 / 250) x 100**.
 
• Performing the calculation: **5 / 250 = 0.02**. Then, **0.02 x 100 = 2**. Therefore, the concentration is **2%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solute**: This is the component of the solution that is dissolved in the solvent and is usually present in a **smaller amount**. In this example, the **5 g** of substance is the solute.
 
• **Solvent**: This is the component of the solution that dissolves the other component and is usually present in a **larger amount** (often water).
 
• **Solution**: A **homogeneous mixture** of two or more substances. The volume of the solution used in the denominator of the **w/v %** formula must represent the **final volume** of the mixture.
 
• **Other Concentration Expressions**:
 
 
• **Mass by Mass Percentage (w/w %)**: Calculated as **(Mass of Solute / Mass of Solution) x 100**.
 
• **Volume by Volume Percentage (v/v %)**: Calculated as **(Volume of Solute / Volume of Solution) x 100**, typically used for liquid-in-liquid solutions like **alcohol in water**.
 
 
 
• **Molarity (M)**: Another vital unit of concentration defined as the **number of moles** of solute per **liter** of solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **units** must be consistent when using the percentage formula. For **mass by volume %**, the standard practice is to use **grams (g)** for mass and **milliliters (mL)** for volume.
 
• A **2% (w/v)** solution means that every **100 mL** of that solution contains **2 g** of the dissolved solute.
 
• In **pharmacology and medicine**, many intravenous fluids and liquid medications are labeled using this **mass by volume percentage** system (e.g., **0.9% Normal Saline**).
 
• If the volume was given in **Liters**, it must be converted to **milliliters** (**1 L = 1000 mL**) before applying the **percentage** formula.
